record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Existence for nonlocal multispecies model with perception
record.original_question: For the nonlocal n-population movement system in which each population u_i satisfies ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(Σ_j=1^n γ_ij u_j g,R)), where g is the detection function and the advection potential is the perceived density of all populations, in what functional setting do time-dependent solutions exist on a bounded domain with periodic boundary conditions? In particular, can existence be proved when the detection function is the biologically important top-hat kernel rather than a smooth kernel such as a Gaussian?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. In what context do solutions exist solving the time-dependent problem (2.10) subject to periodic boundary conditions in a bounded domain? In [23], a partial answer is established when the detection function g(·) is twice continuously differentiable (e.g., the Gaussian detection function), but few results exist for the top-hat detection function.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider $n$ population densities $u_1,\dots,u_n:\Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ on a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with periodic boundary conditions. For each $i=1,\dots,n$, let $u_i$ satisfy the nonlocal advection–diffusion system
$$\partial_t u_i \;=\; d_i\,\Delta u_i \;-\; \nabla\!\cdot\!\Big( u_i\,\nabla\Big[\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma_{ij}\, (u_j * g_R)\Big]\Big), \qquad i=1,\dots,n,$$
where $d_i>0$ are diffusion coefficients, $\gamma_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}$ are interspecies sensitivity coefficients, and the perceived density is given by the spatial convolution
$$(u_j * g_R)(x,t) \;=\; \int_\Omega g_R(x-y)\, u_j(y,t)\,dy,$$
with $g_R$ a nonnegative radially symmetric detection kernel of perceptual range $R>0$, normalized so that $\int g_R = 1$. Initial data $u_i(\cdot,0) = u_i^0\ge 0$ are prescribed.

(a) Identify a functional setting (function spaces for initial data and for the solution map) in which time-dependent (local and/or global) classical or weak solutions to this system exist.

(b) In particular, establish existence of solutions when $g_R$ is the top-hat kernel
$$g_R(x) \;=\; \frac{1}{|B_R(0)|}\,\mathbf{1}_{\{|x|\le R\}},$$
which is merely bounded and discontinuous, rather than the case of a smooth kernel (such as a Gaussian) for which $g\in C^2$.
artifact.status_search_result: Local and global existence results have been established for the smooth-kernel case (Giunta–Hillen–Lewis–Potts, SIADS 2022). For the more delicate top-hat detection kernel, subsequent works prove existence and uniqueness of (Hölder continuous / weak) global solutions in one spatial dimension, including discontinuous kernels (e.g., arXiv:2312.09692, 2024). Higher-dimensional existence with the top-hat kernel remains only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Local and Global Existence for Nonlocal Multispecies Advection-Diffusion Models
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theorems have been proven for a class of nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion models... Global existence has been proven for models in 1 spatial dimension and local existence for higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Smooth-kernel case is addressed; global existence in 1D, local in higher D.

status_evidence.title: Positivity and global existence for nonlocal advection-diffusion models of interacting populations
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and uniqueness of global weak solutions in one spatial dimension using an iterative approach, including potentially discontinuous detection kernels like the top-hat detection function.
status_evidence.claim: Top-hat kernel case resolved in 1D via weak solution framework.
